text:
Devon C: Heads up — saw a regression after yesterday's router change. p95 for the mixed-model path (fallback to M-family) is up ~22% when draft routing is enabled. profiler attached below.

perf-bot: alert: latency_regression service=runtime path=mixed-fallback env=prod delta_p95=22%

Anya P: can you paste the profiler snippet? is this with speculative drafts only or all decodes? :eyes:

Devon C: only when draft routing + draft-accept tuning is active. normal decode path unaffected. quick dump:

```
# top stacks by time (sampled)
- tokenization.normalize: 18.7%  (mixed tokenizer path)
- attention.kv_write: 16.4%  (increased writes on fallback)
- compile.select_kernels: 12.1% (fallback picks slower kernels for M variants)
- scheduler.batch_wait: 9.8% (more frequent micro-batching due to acceptance hysteresis)
- decoding.spec_check: 7.3% (draft accept checks)
```

Devon C: also seeing KV cache miss rate jump from 2.3% -> 11.8% for these sessions. seems like head/kv dim mismatch + tokenizer differences cause cache keys not to match cached prefixes.

Samir: interesting. do we know whether RoPE scaling mismatch could cause recompute of attention matrices and thus the writes?

Irene: yes, if fallback model has different RoPE base or head count we end up reconstructing KV per-token. that can turn a fast prefix-cache hit into a full re-emit. add to hypothesis list: tokenizer normalization, head dim mismatch, ropemult mismatch.

Anya P: any repro harness? we should get a minimal script to reproduce deterministically. Samir / Irene, can you run quick bench with draft=on and forced fallback to M-family?

Samir: running now. command I used: `./bench/run_infer --model=mix-run-v3 --force-fallback=M-v2 --draft=true --seq=512 --iter=200`

Samir: results (canary run): p50=48ms, p95=210ms (draft off p95=170ms). acceptance rate observed 0.42 -> 0.58 depending on prompt seed. KV miss ratio matches Devon's numbers.

Devon C: workaround idea: make router pre-tokenize everything before acceptance decision and normalize token ids against target model vocab. that way acceptance logic uses canonical token ids and we avoid cache mismatches. downside: extra CPU and latency before routing.

Irene: alternative quick mitigation: for any fallback where vocab or rope base differs, avoid using prefix-KV cache and instead serve with a cold-kv policy (slower but consistent). we can implement a selective prefix_disable flag at routing time: `routing.disable_prefix_cache_for_fallback: true`

Samir: proposed short-term config to roll (canary):
```
models:
  M-family:
    draft_accept_threshold: 0.55
    runtime_hints:
      prefer_exact_vocab: true
      disable_prefix_cache_on_mismatch: true
```

Anya P: I like the controlled threshold change + disable cache fallback. reduces speculative acceptance, so fewer cases exercise the mismatch. But this will increase p50 for some prompts. tradeoff acknowledged.

Devon C: I've opened a quick PR to the router that adds `vocab_fingerprint` check during handshake and returns `cache_ok: false` in the routing decision when mismatch detected. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pull/712 :shipit:

perf-bot: deploy started: router-canary-712 -> prod/zone-a

Samir: monitoring dashboards set: runtime/mixed-fallback/p95, kv_miss_rate, draft_accept_rate. I'll post graphs in 10m.

Irene: long-term fix: we should align tokenizer normalization across family variants during model onboarding, and include `rope_base` + `head_dim` in the model compatibility metadata so the router can make smarter pairing decisions. also consider a precompute step to map prefix token ids between vocab spaces where feasible.

Anya P: agreed. add a follow-up ticket for onboarding + compatibility metadata. Devon/ Samir, can you capture the repro steps and attach to the ticket?

Devon C: done — ticket INF-1293 with repro script + profiles. putting the temporary canary config in place now.

Samir: canary looks healthy so far, p95 down to 183ms (from 210). KV miss rate trending down. will keep an eye for 30m window.

Irene: note for postmortem: acceptance tuning interacts badly with heterogeneous family fallbacks. need automated test in perf harness that exercises cross-family draft routing.

Devon C: thanks all. follow-up sync tomorrow to decide whether to keep `disable_prefix_cache_on_mismatch` or invest in token-id translation. cc @Anya P :thumbsup:

Anya P: thanks. keeping this thread for updates. :eyes:
